dwp_take: Photon just raised 4.5 million dollars to build AI agents that live in your messaging apps instead of requiring you to download yet another standalone app. For digital workplace professionals, this matters because it signals a real shift in how organizations might deliver employee tools, services, and automation without the deployment and update headaches of traditional apps. Honestly, after three decades watching companies struggle to get people to use their internal apps, I'm cautiously optimistic about anything that reduces friction, though I'll believe it when I see actual enterprise adoption.

title: Hearing tech startup Legato launches its AI hearing glasses
excerpt: The glasses stem from the startup’s goal of making hearing care more accessible by addressing the cost, comfort, and stigma associated with traditional hearing aids.
dwp_take: Legato, a hearing tech startup, just launched AI-powered glasses designed to make hearing assistance more affordable and less socially awkward than traditional hearing aids. This matters to digital workplace pros because accessibility tools that actually get used are the difference between inclusive workplaces and well-intentioned policies nobody touches. Look, if we can finally kill the stigma around hearing aids by disguising them as something people already want to wear, we've solved a problem that's been sitting on the shelf for twenty years.

title: Who owns AI risk at work? Business and tech leaders can’t agree, PwC survey finds
excerpt: PwC research highlights a growing need for someone to own AI. Is an AI chief the answer?
dwp_take: PwC surveyed business and tech leaders and found they can't agree on who should be responsible for managing AI risk in their organizations. This matters because without clear ownership, AI implementation becomes a scattered mess where everyone blames someone else when things go wrong, and critical safeguards fall through the cracks. Here's the thing: companies don't need another chief officer with a fancy title. They need to assign accountability to actual humans with real consequences, whether that's the CTO, legal, or whoever's already got skin in the game.

title: Forget flexibility. Working parents need predictability
excerpt: For years, we have believed that flexibility is the key to survival for working parents. We advocate for flexible hours, flexible PTO, flexible locations. And the ability to log on from the pediatrici
dwp_take: Microsoft's latest research shows that working parents actually crave predictability over flexibility, finding that the ability to know their schedule in advance matters more than having the option to work anywhere anytime. This matters because most digital workplace strategies over the past decade have been built around maximum flexibility, which paradoxically creates chaos for people juggling school calendars and childcare. The real takeaway is that we've spent years offering people keys to invisible offices while they actually needed someone to just tell them when they'd be free.
